name: Step-by-Step Garage Floor Coating Application for Colorado Homes

step.name: Step 1: Clear the garage slab completely
step.text: Empty every item, storage cabinet, tool chest, and vehicle out of the garage workspace. Check the entire concrete perimeter to make sure work crews have full, unrestricted access to all floor edges and corners. A fully emptied room is essential so dust and prep debris do not settle onto stored belongings.

step.name: Step 2: Degrease stains and strip old surface coatings
step.text: Inspect the entire concrete floor for engine fluids, wax, tire marks, and previous coats of paint or sealer. Apply a targeted industrial degreaser to lift oil spots, and scrape or strip away any peeling, incompatible paints. Done properly, the bare concrete is free of slick spots that would block new coating adhesion.

step.name: Step 3: Patch cracks, pitting, and spalled concrete
step.text: Fill all visible slab cracks, pits, and rough spalls using a compatible concrete repair compound. Smooth the patching compound flush with the surrounding floor so there are no uneven ridges or low voids. The repair material must fully harden before you move forward to surface profiling.

step.name: Step 4: Profile or etch the concrete surface mechanically
step.text: Abrade the concrete slab using mechanical diamond grinding or an approved etching solution to create an open, porous profile. Remove all loose dust, slurry, and grit by vacuuming the entire floor thoroughly. When complete, the concrete feels like medium-grit sandpaper and readily absorbs water droplets.

step.name: Step 5: Apply the base coating layers within proper temperature limits
step.text: Verify the ambient and slab temperatures sit safely between 40°F and 90°F before mixing your coating resins with hardener. Spread the base layer evenly across the slab using a squeegee and roller, working methodically from the back wall toward the open garage door.

step.name: Step 6: Protect the floor and manage the curing window
step.text: Keep pets, foot traffic, and outdoor debris off the wet floor while the coating hardens into a durable surface. Keep foot traffic off for at least 24 hours, and hold off on parking vehicles for 24 to 36 hours, extending up to 96 or 120 hours in colder weather.
